gloss: way of cutting; cutting technique; how to cut

definitions.gloss: way of cutting; cutting technique; how to cut
definitions.explanation: The method or manner of cutting something — typically food in a cooking context, but also paper, fabric, or hair. Formed by the verb {切|き}る (to cut) + {方|かた} (way of doing).

examples.japanese: {玉|たま}ねぎの{切|き}り{方|かた}を{教|おし}えて。
examples.english: Teach me how to cut an onion.

examples.japanese: {食材|しょくざい}の{切|き}り{方|かた}で{料理|りょうり}の{味|あじ}が{変|か}わる。
examples.english: How you cut the ingredients changes the taste of the dish.

examples.japanese: {刺身|さしみ}は{切|き}り{方|かた}{一|ひと}つで{食感|しょっかん}も{見|み}た{目|め}も{大|おお}きく{変|か}わる。
examples.english: With sashimi, just a change in how you cut it can dramatically alter the texture and appearance.

notes:
An instance of the productive verb-stem + {方|かた} pattern meaning "way of doing X" (cf. {食|た}べ{方|かた} "way of eating," {書|か}き{方|かた} "way of writing"). Most commonly used in cooking, where the cutting technique has a named system of styles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {切|き}り{方|かた}を{教|おし}える: to teach someone how to cut
- {切|き}り{方|かた}を{覚|おぼ}える: to learn how to cut
- {正|ただ}しい{切|き}り{方|かた}: the correct cutting method

CUTTING STYLES (examples):
- みじん{切|ぎ}り: fine mince
- せん{切|ぎ}り: julienne
- {輪切|わぎ}り: round slices
- {薄|うす}{切|ぎ}り: thin slices
- {乱切|らんぎ}り: random/rolling cut
